title: Sixty-three years, 34 moments
lede: From a beachfront pancake house to a covered sign. Filter by thread.

events.title: The first restaurant opens
events.text: Sam Battistone and F. Newell Bohnett open a pancake house at 216 West Cabrillo Boulevard, Santa Barbara.

events.title: Fraction of the Action begins
events.text: Managers can buy 20% of their restaurant for $20,000. The chain has 67 restaurants.

events.title: Sambo’s goes public
events.text: The shares are split five times between 1970 and 1974.

events.title: Ann Arbor application
events.text: The company files a site plan for a restaurant in Ann Arbor, Michigan. Council members and the mayor object to the name.

events.title: The first Jolly Tiger
events.text: Ann Arbor approves the restaurant after the company agrees not to use the name Sambo’s there.

events.title: The peak year
events.text: 869 restaurants, income of $22.8M and a share price that touches 27.

events.title: The SEC objects
events.text: The commission says managers’ payments cannot be recorded as sales. The company restates 20 years of earnings and replaces the plan.

events.title: Under fire in New England
events.text: The Times reports pickets, a suit by the Massachusetts attorney general and a license refused in Reading. Nine-month earnings have fallen to $3.1M from $6.8M.

events.title: Rhode Island complaint
events.text: The Urban League of Rhode Island, the local NAACP and two individuals complain to the state human rights commission.

events.title: Losses begin
events.text: Sambo’s loses money in the fourth quarter and never reports another profit.

events.title: Shareholder revolt
events.text: Dissident shareholders almost elect two directors.

events.title: Battistone Sr. steps down
events.text: Creditors press for four outside directors. The founder, 69, resigns as chairman and is replaced by his son, Sam D. Battistone, 39.

events.title: The Motel 6 team arrives
events.text: GDV, a unit of City Investing, pays $13.7M for a 16% holding and installs Daniel R. Shaughnessy as president. The chain has 1,090 restaurants.

events.title: $77.8M loss
events.text: The loss for the year, as UPI later reported it. More than 70% of managers have resigned in two years.

events.title: City Investing reaches 34%
events.text: The conglomerate completes its purchase of 34% of the chain for $29M. The loss for the year is $11.6M.

events.title: Suing the founders
events.text: New management files a $100M suit against 28 former officials, including Battistone and Bohnett.

events.title: No Place Like Sam’s
events.text: The company renames 18 restaurants in Massachusetts, Connecticut and New Hampshire. It has 1,117 restaurants.

events.title: Rhode Island order
events.text: The Commission for Human Rights orders the four Rhode Island restaurants renamed. The company says it will appeal.

events.title: $925,000 verdict
events.text: An Oregon court awards damages to a former manager who sued for fraud over the profit-sharing plan.

events.title: Default
events.text: Sambo’s misses a $4.8M payment, the first installment of a $100M restructured loan from 17 lenders.

events.title: Sixth Circuit rules for the name
events.text: The court of appeals orders Ann Arbor to let the restaurant use the name Sambo’s.

events.title: Closings begin
events.text: Restaurants in Michigan, Ohio and Kentucky shut first. Until then the new management had closed only five or six.

events.title: 447 closed, shares halted
events.text: The company says it has closed 447 restaurants and sold 12, leaving 667. Five men, including two former officers, are indicted for fraud.

events.title: Chapter 11
events.text: Sambo’s Restaurants Inc. files a voluntary petition in the Central District of California.

events.title: Season’s
events.text: With $30M borrowed from GDV and the Foothill Group, more than 600 restaurants are converted to a new format and name.

events.title: Examiner’s warning
events.text: A court examiner says Season’s needs a sharper rise in sales. The company sells 250 restaurants and agrees to convert 112 to Godfather’s Pizza.

events.title: A third format
events.text: Sambo’s says it may turn its remaining 320 Season’s restaurants into Coco’s and Baxter’s franchises for W.R. Grace.

events.title: Vicorp buys 166
events.text: The trustee and Vicorp announce a court-approved sale for $54.8M: 107 restaurants in California, 46 in Florida, 9 in Arizona and 4 elsewhere.

events.title: The family buys back the first one
events.text: After selling the Utah Jazz in 1985–86, Sam D. Battistone persuades Vicorp to sell him the Santa Barbara restaurant. The exact date is not in our sources.

events.title: Registration canceled
events.text: The federal trademark registration filed by the company in October 1981 is canceled for want of a renewal declaration.

events.title: Talk of a revival
events.text: Chad Stevens, the founder’s grandson, tells the Los Angeles Times and CNN he wants to relaunch the chain under its old name.

events.title: A new trademark application
events.text: Palm Beach Restaurants, Inc. of Santa Barbara applies to register the name for restaurant services. The application is abandoned on October 21.

events.title: The sign is covered
events.text: After a petition by Rashelle Monet, the owners cover the letters with a peace symbol and the words “& LOVE.”

events.title: Chad’s
events.text: A new sign goes up on the building after 63 years.
